newsitem.title: UK: N.Sea Brent intermonth spreads, CFDs trade weaker.
newsitem.headline: N.Sea Brent intermonth spreads, CFDs trade weaker.

text.p: North Sea Brent paper markets eased on Friday, flagging a weakening of values for Dated Brent, traders said.
Intermonth spreads were well offered across the forward curve, with one Wall Street trader a particularly aggressive seller, paper dealers said.
"They're keen to sell the spreads," said one.
Mar/Apr was talked at +33/36, having traded at +42 and +40 in the U.S. aftermarket. Apr/May traded twice at +25 cents down five cents from Thursday's traded levels.
CFDs were also under pressure. Next week (Feb 24-28) was talked at April Brent +27/30, while the following week (March 3-7) was traded at +17 cents.
Outright Brent values fell, with April Brent trading 20 cents down at $19.88 a barrel at 1050 GMT on the IPE, the first time the spot contract has slipped below $20 since last August.

Three cargoes from the original March Brent loading programme were to be nominated from the paper chains on Friday. Traders said that top-up barrels in the March 8-10 window might also be put together to make another cargo.

Dated Brent was last reported traded on Wednesday at March Brent -2 cents. Offers for March 1-3 barrels were seen at March Brent -8 cents on Thursday, but bids for later first decade Brent were seen at March -3 cents, dealers said.
